User: Here is the information on hash tables:
<p>For an introduction to Hashing and Hash Tables - <a href="https://thispointer.com/what-is-hashing-and-hash-table/">https://thispointer.com/what-is-hashing-and-hash-table/</a></p>
<p>A <strong>hash function</strong> is "<em>any function that can be used to map data of arbitrary size onto data of a fixed size."</em> (<a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hash_function">https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hash_function</a>)</p>
<p>Our main interest in hashing is the creation and use of hash tables.</p>
<p>"<em>A <strong>hash table</strong> (<strong>hash map</strong>) is a data structure that implements an associative array abstract data type, a structure that can map keys to values. A hash table uses a hash function to compute an index into an array of buckets or slots, from which the desired value can be found.</em>" (<a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hash_table">https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hash_table</a>)</p>
<p>In the example provided in the introduction link above, all numbers were split and placed into one of 10 bins. Anytime a bin has more than 1 element in it, that is called a collision. To search and see if a number is already stored in your hash table, you would first hash the number you are looking for, then go to the bin where that number would be stored and search through what is stored in that bin. For a set of random numbers, this means that, on average, you would search through 1/2 of 1/10 of the total number of things stored in that hash table.</p>
<p>In an ideal world, every bin would only have 1 item in it - this is called a "Perfect Hash". In reality, this isn't possible so you will always have collisions to deal with. The basic structure of a hash table is an Array of Linked-Lists where the Array Indices are the "Bins" and the values stored in each Bin are stored in a Linked-List (essentially this is the same as a Graph except coded to store and retrieve data).</p>
<p>This video provides a nice overview/introduction into how hash tables work and how you can implement them.</p>
<p><a class="" href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dsuxijrK-EQ" data-preview-alt="C++ Tutorial: Intro to Hash Tables">C++ Tutorial: Intro to Hash Tables</a></p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p>What's a Hash Table:</p>
<p>Simple overview of Hash Table and Hashing - <a href="https://thispointer.com/what-is-hashing-and-hash-table/">https://thispointer.com/what-is-hashing-and-hash-table/</a></p>
<p>Tutorial on creating a hash table in c++ (needs to be reworked because some issues with structure) - <a class="" href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m6n_rozU8dA" data-preview-alt="How to Create A Hash Table Project in C++ , Part 1 , Setting Up the Hash Table Project">How to Create A Hash Table Project in C++ , Part 1 , Setting Up the Hash Table Project</a>&nbsp;</p>
<p>Most secure Cryptographic Hash as of 4/7/2022 is: SHA-256</p>
<p><a class="inline_disabled" href="https://www.simplilearn.com/tutorials/cyber-security-tutorial/sha-256-algorithm#what_is_the_sha256_algorithm" target="_blank" rel="noopener">The SHA-256 Algorithm Explained</a></p>
<p><a class="inline_disabled" href="https://sha256algorithm.com/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">SHA-256 Algorithm in Action</a></p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>Good video on How/Why we use Hashing Algorithms</p>
<p><a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b4b8ktEV4Bg" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Hashing Algorithms and Security - Computerphile</a></p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p>Modify the included game program using the defined hashing function to:</p>
<ul>
<li>Hash the user's guess and compare it to the value to be found.</li>
<li>When found, report out the following:
<ul>
<li>Original value to be guessed</li>
<li>Hashed value to be guessed</li>
<li>Final Guess</li>
<li>Hashed value of final guess</li>
<li>How many tries it took to guess the value</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<p>Guessing Game Code: <a class="instructure_file_link instructure_scribd_file inline_disabled" title="guess.cpp" href="https://mendocino.instructure.com/courses/21391/files/2621474?wrap=1" target="_blank" rel="noopener" data-api-endpoint="https://mendocino.instructure.com/api/v1/courses/21391/files/2621474" data-api-returntype="File">guess.cpp</a></p>
<p>Hashing Function:</p>
<p style="padding-left: 40px;">h(k) = floor (M (FkA mod 1))</p>
<p style="padding-left: 40px;">where:</p>
<p style="padding-left: 40px;">M = 9.9</p>
<p style="padding-left: 40px;">F = 12345</p>
<p style="padding-left: 40px;">k = guess or value</p>
<p style="padding-left: 40px;">A = 0.323323</p>
<p style="padding-left: 40px;">h(k) = hashed value</p>

</ul>
<p>Once you've created the Hash table of colors, have your program do the following:</p>
<ul>
<li>Report out the:
<ul>
<li>Average number of colors stored in each bin ignoring any bins that have 0 entries</li>
<li>Maximum number of colors in any one bin</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>Write a loop that continues until the user says stop that:
<ul>
<li>Asks the user to search for a color
<ul>
<li>If found, ignoring the case, report which bin it was found in (Make sure your code ONLY searches the appropriate bin)</li>
<li>If not found, add the color to the Hash Table</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>

<h4 dir="ltr" style="text-align: left; font-size: 20px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="20">Open Addressing</h4>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16"><em>Another approach to collisions:&nbsp;</em></p>
<ul dir="ltr">
    <li style="text-align: left; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16">no chaining; instead all items stored in table (see Fig. 1)</li>

padding-left: 0.201em;">ℎ</span><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-36" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular;">(</span><span class="mi" id="MathJax-Span-37" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Italic;">𝑘</span><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-38" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular;">,</span><span class="mi" id="MathJax-Span-39" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Italic; padding-left: 0.201em;">𝑚</span><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-40" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular; padding-left: 0.25em;">−</span><span class="mn" id="MathJax-Span-41" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular; padding-left: 0.25em;">1</span><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-42" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular;">)</span><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-43" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular;">⟩</span></span><span style="display: inline-block; width: 0px; height: 2.284em;"></span></span></span><span style="display: inline-block; overflow: hidden; vertical-align: -0.309em; border-left: 0px solid; width: 0px; height: 1.316em;"></span></span></nobr><span class="MJX_Assistive_MathML" role="presentation"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo stretchy="false">〈</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">〉</mo></math></span></span><script type="math/tex" id="MathJax-Element-4"> 〈h(k, 0), h(k, 1), . . . , h(k, m − 1)〉 </script></span><br></p>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16">is a permutation of <span class="nolink" data-asw-orgfontsize="16" style="font-size: 16px;"><span class="MathJax_Preview" style="color: inherit;"></span><span class="MathJax" id="MathJax-Element-5-Frame" tabindex="0" data-mathml="&lt;math xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML&quot;&gt;&lt;mn&gt;0&lt;/mn&gt;&lt;mo&gt;,&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;mn&gt;1&lt;/mn&gt;&lt;mo&gt;,&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;mo&gt;.&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;mo&gt;.&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;mo&gt;.&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;mo&gt;,&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;mi&gt;m&lt;/mi&gt;&lt;mo&gt;&amp;#x2212;&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;mn&gt;1&lt;/mn&gt;&lt;/math&gt;" role="presentation" style="position: relative;"><nobr aria-hidden="true"><span class="math" id="MathJax-Span-44" style="width: 7.691em; display: inline-block;"><span style="display: inline-block; position: relative; width: 6.104em; height: 0px; font-size: 126%;"><span style="position: absolute; clip: rect(1.441em, 1006em, 2.582em, -999.998em); top: -2.279em; left: 0em;"><span class="mrow" id="MathJax-Span-45"><span class="mn" id="MathJax-Span-46" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular;">0</span><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-47" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular;">,</span><span class="mn" id="MathJax-Span-48" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular; padding-left: 0.201em;">1</span><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-49" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular;">,</span><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-50" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular; padding-left: 0.201em;">.</span><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-51" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular; padding-left: 0.201em;">,</span><span class="mi" id="MathJax-Span-54" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Italic; padding-left: 0.201em;">𝑚</span><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-55" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular; padding-left: 0.25em;">−</span><span class="mn" id="MathJax-Span-56" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular; padding-left: 0.25em;">1</span></span><span style="display: inline-block; width: 0px; height: 2.284em;"></span></span></span><span style="display: inline-block; overflow: hidden; vertical-align: -0.247em; border-left: 0px solid; width: 0px; height: 1.128em;"></span></span></nobr><span class="MJX_Assistive_MathML" role="presentation"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></math></span></span><script type="math/tex" id="MathJax-Element-5">0, 1, . . . , m − 1</script></span>. i.e. if I keep trying <span class="nolink" data-asw-orgfontsize="16" style="font-size: 16px;"><span class="MathJax_Preview" style="color: inherit;"></span><span class="MathJax" id="MathJax-Element-6-Frame" tabindex="0" data-mathml="&lt;math xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML&quot;&gt;&lt;mi&gt;h&lt;/mi&gt;&lt;mo stretchy=&quot;false&quot;&gt;(&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;mi&gt;k&lt;/mi&gt;&lt;mo&gt;,&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;mi&gt;i&lt;/mi&gt;&lt;mo stretchy=&quot;false&quot;&gt;)&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;/math&gt;" role="presentation" style="position: relative;"><nobr aria-hidden="true"><span class="math" id="MathJax-Span-57" style="width: 3.078em; display: inline-block;"><span style="display: inline-block; position: relative; width: 2.433em; height: 0px; font-size: 126%;"><span style="position: absolute; clip: rect(1.441em, 1002.38em, 2.631em, -999.998em); top: -2.279em; left: 0em;"><span class="mrow" id="MathJax-Span-58"><span class="mi" id="MathJax-Span-59" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Italic;">ℎ</span><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-60" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular;">(</span><span class="mi" id="MathJax-Span-61" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Italic;">𝑘</span><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-62" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular;">,</span><span class="mi" id="MathJax-Span-63" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Italic; padding-left: 0.201em;">𝑖</span><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-64" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular;">)</span></span><span style="display: inline-block; width: 0px; height: 2.284em;"></span></span></span><span style="display: inline-block; overflow: hidden; vertical-align: -0.309em; border-left: 0px solid; width: 0px; height: 1.191em;"></span></span></nobr><span class="MJX_Assistive_MathML" role="presentation"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math></span></span><script type="math/tex" id="MathJax-Element-6">h(k, i)</script></span> for increasing <em>i</em>,
    I will eventually hit all slots of the table.<br></p>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: center; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16"><img src="https://learn.saylor.org/pluginfile.php/10439572/mod_book/chapter/90524/Screenshot%202024-04-27%20at%2009-03-27%206.006%20Lecture%2010%20Open%20addressing%20cryptographic%20hashing%20-%20a7f609148928e4a10653d3f3be03a2b5_MIT6_006F11_lec10.pdf.png" alt="Figure 2: Order of Probes" width="286" height="300" class="img-fluid atto_image_button_text-bottom"><br></p>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: center; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16"><strong>Figure 2: </strong>Order of Probes</p>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16"><strong>Insert(k,v)</strong>: Keep probing until an empty slot is found. Insert item into that slot.&nbsp;</p>
<pre class="prettyprint"><em>for i in xrange(m):<br>if T [h(k, i)] is None: //empty slot<br>T [h(k, i)] = (k, v) ]&nbsp; //store item<br>return<br>raise 'full'&nbsp;</em></pre>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16">Example: Insert k = 496</p>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16"><strong>Search(k)</strong>: As long as the slots you encounter by probing are occupied by keys&nbsp;≠ k,
    keep probing until you either encounter k or find an empty slot - return success or
    failure respectively.&nbsp;</p>
<pre class="prettyprint"><em>for i in xrange(m):<br>if T [h(k, i)] is None:&nbsp; //empty slot?<br>return None //end of "chain"<br>elif T [h(k, i)][∅] == k:&nbsp; //matching key<br>return T [h(k, i)]&nbsp; //return item<br>return None //exhausted table</em><br></pre>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: center; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16"><img src="https://learn.saylor.org/pluginfile.php/10439572/mod_book/chapter/90524/Screenshot%202024-04-27%20at%2009-05-42%206.006%20Lecture%2010%20Open%20addressing%20cryptographic%20hashing%20-%20a7f609148928e4a10653d3f3be03a2b5_MIT6_006F11_lec10.pdf.png" alt="Figure 3: Insert Example" width="386" height="269" class="img-fluid atto_image_button_text-bottom"><br></p>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: center; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16"><strong>Figure 3:</strong> Insert Example</p>
<h5 dir="ltr" style="text-align: left; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16">Deleting Items?</h5>
<ul dir="ltr">
    <li style="text-align: left; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16">can't just find item and remove it from its slot (i.e. set T [h(k, i)] = None)</li>
    <li style="text-align: left; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16">example: delete(586) =⇒ search(496) fails</li>
    <li style="text-align: left; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16">replace item with special flag: "DeleteMe", which Insert treats as None but
        Search doesn't&nbsp;</li>
</ul>
<h5 dir="ltr" style="text-align: left; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16">Probing Strategies</h5>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16">Linear Probing</p>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16"><span class="nolink" data-asw-orgfontsize="16" style="font-size: 16px;"><span class="MathJax_Preview" style="color: inherit;"></span><span class="MathJax" id="MathJax-Element-7-Frame" tabindex="0" data-mathml="&lt;math xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML&quot;&gt;&lt;mi&gt;h&lt;/mi&gt;&lt;mo stretchy=&quot;false&quot;&gt;(&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;mi&gt;k&lt;/mi&gt;&lt;mo&gt;,&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;mi&gt;i&lt;/mi&gt;&lt;mo stretchy=&quot;false&quot;&gt;)&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;mo&gt;=&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;mo stretchy=&quot;false&quot;&gt;(&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;mi&gt;h&lt;/mi&gt;&lt;mrow class=&quot;MJX-TeXAtom-ORD&quot;&gt;&lt;mo&gt;&amp;#x2032;&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;/mrow&gt;&lt;mo stretchy=&quot;false&quot;&gt;(&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;mi&gt;k&lt;/mi&gt;&lt;mo stretchy=&quot;false&quot;&gt;)&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;mo&gt;+&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;mi&gt;i&lt;/mi&gt;&lt;mo stretchy=&quot;false&quot;&gt;)&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;mtext&gt;&amp;#xA0;mod&amp;#xA0;&lt;/mtext&gt;&lt;mi&gt;m&lt;/mi&gt;&lt;/math&gt;" role="presentation" style="position: relative;"><nobr aria-hidden="true"><span class="math" id="MathJax-Span-65" style="width: 13.395em; display: inline-block;"><span style="display: inline-block; position: relative; width: 10.618em; height: 0px; font-size: 126%;"><span style="position: absolute; clip: rect(1.441em, 1010.57em, 2.631em, -999.998em); top: -2.279em; left: 0em;"><span class="mrow" id="MathJax-Span-66"><span class="mi" id="MathJax-Span-67" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Italic;">ℎ</span><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-68" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular;">(</span><span class="mi" id="MathJax-Span-69" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Italic;">𝑘</span><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-70" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular;">,</span><span class="mi" id="MathJax-Span-71" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Italic; padding-left: 0.3em;">(</span><span class="mi" id="MathJax-Span-75" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Italic;">ℎ</span><span class="texatom" id="MathJax-Span-76"><span class="mrow" id="MathJax-Span-77"><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-78" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular;">′</span></span></span><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-79" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular;">(</span><span class="mi" id="MathJax-Span-80" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Italic;">𝑘</span><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-81" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular;">)</span><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-82" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular; padding-left: 0.25em;">+</span><span class="mi" id="MathJax-Span-83" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Italic; padding-left: 0.25em;">𝑖</span><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-84" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular;">)</span><span class="mtext" id="MathJax-Span-85" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular;">&nbsp;mod&nbsp;</span><span class="mi" id="MathJax-Span-86" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Italic;">𝑚</span></span><span style="display: inline-block; width: 0px; height: 2.284em;"></span></span></span><span style="display: inline-block; overflow: hidden; vertical-align: -0.309em; border-left: 0px solid; width: 0px; height: 1.191em;"></span></span></nobr><span class="MJX_Assistive_MathML" role="presentation"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"><mo>′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mtext>&nbsp;mod&nbsp;</mtext><mi>m</mi></math></span></span><script type="math/tex" id="MathJax-Element-7">h(k, i) = (h′(k) +i) \text{ mod }m</script></span> where <em>h′(k)</em> is ordinary hash function</p>
<ul dir="ltr">
    <li style="text-align: left; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16">like street parking</li>
    <li style="text-align: left; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16">problem? <em>clustering </em>- cluster: consecutive group of occupied slots
        as clusters become longer, it gets more likely to grow further (see Fig. 4)</li>
    <li style="text-align: left; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16">can be shown that for <span class="nolink" data-asw-orgfontsize="16" style="font-size: 16px;"><span class="MathJax_Preview" style="color: inherit;"></span><span class="MathJax" id="MathJax-Element-8-Frame" tabindex="0" data-mathml="&lt;math xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML&quot;&gt;&lt;mn&gt;0.01&lt;/mn&gt;&lt;mo&gt;&amp;lt;&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;mrow class=&quot;MJX-TeXAtom-ORD&quot;&gt;&lt;mo&gt;&amp;#x3B1;&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;/mrow&gt;&lt;mo&gt;&amp;lt;&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;mn&gt;0.99&lt;/mn&gt;&lt;/math&gt;" role="presentation" style="position: relative;"><nobr aria-hidden="true"><span class="math" id="MathJax-Span-87" style="width: 8.137em; <h4 dir="ltr" style="text-align: left; font-size: 20px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="20"><br></h4><h4 dir="ltr" style="text-align: left; font-size: 20px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="20">Double Hashing</h4>

width: 0px; height: 2.383em;"></span></span></span><span style="display: inline-block; overflow: hidden; vertical-align: -0.309em; border-left: 0px solid; width: 0px; height: 1.253em;"></span></span></nobr><span class="MJX_Assistive_MathML" role="presentation"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>·</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mtext>&nbsp;mod&nbsp;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>j</mi><mo>·</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mtext>&nbsp;mod&nbsp;</mtext><mi>m</mi></math></span></span><script type="math/tex" id="MathJax-Element-14">h_1(k) + i · h_2(k) \text { mod }m = h_1(k) + j · h_2(k) \text{ mod }m </script></span> ⇒ <em>m divides (i − j)</em></p>
</div>
<ul dir="ltr">
    <li style="text-align: left; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16">e.g. <span class="nolink" data-asw-orgfontsize="16" style="font-size: 16px;"><span class="MathJax_Preview" style="color: inherit;"></span><span class="MathJax" id="MathJax-Element-15-Frame" tabindex="0" data-mathml="&lt;math xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML&quot;&gt;&lt;mi&gt;m&lt;/mi&gt;&lt;mo&gt;=&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;msup&gt;&lt;mn&gt;2&lt;/mn&gt;&lt;mi&gt;r&lt;/mi&gt;&lt;/msup&gt;&lt;/math&gt;" role="presentation" style="position: relative;"><nobr aria-hidden="true"><span class="math" id="MathJax-Span-197" style="width: 3.574em; </ul><br>
<h4 dir="ltr" style="text-align: left; font-size: 20px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="20">Uniform Hashing Assumption (cf. Simple Uniform Hashing
    Assumption)</h4>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16">Each key is equally likely to have any one of the <em>m!</em> permutations as its probe sequence&nbsp;</p>
<ul dir="ltr">
    <li style="text-align: left; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16">not really true&nbsp;</li>
    <li style="text-align: left; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16">but double hashing can come close</li>
</ul>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16"><br></p>
<h3 dir="ltr" style="text-align: left; font-size: 24px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="24">Analysis</h3>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16">Suppose we have used open addressing to insert <span class="nolink" data-asw-orgfontsize="16" style="font-size: 16px;"><span class="MathJax_Preview" style="color: inherit;"></span><span class="MathJax" id="MathJax-Element-17-Frame" tabindex="0" data-mathml="&lt;math xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML&quot;&gt;&lt;mi&gt;n&lt;/mi&gt;&lt;/math&gt;" role="presentation" style="position: relative;"><nobr aria-hidden="true"><span class="math" id="MathJax-Span-212" style="width: 0.697em; Under the uniform hashing assumption the next operation has expected cost of <span class="nolink" data-asw-orgfontsize="16" style="font-size: 16px;"><span class="MathJax_Preview" style="color: inherit;"></span><span class="MathJax" id="MathJax-Element-19-Frame" tabindex="0" data-mathml="&lt;math xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML&quot;&gt;&lt;mo&gt;&amp;#x2264;&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;mstyle displaystyle=&quot;true&quot; <p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16">Example: α = 90% ⇒ 10 expected probes</p><p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16"><br></p>
<h5 dir="ltr" style="text-align: left; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16">Proof:</h5>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16">Suppose we want to insert an item with key <em>k</em>. Suppose that the item is not in the
    table.&nbsp;</p>
<ul dir="ltr">
    <li style="text-align: left; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16">probability first probe successful: <span class="nolink" data-asw-orgfontsize="16" style="font-size: 16px;"><span class="MathJax_Preview" style="color: inherit;"></span><span class="MathJax" id="MathJax-Element-21-Frame" tabindex="0" data-mathml="&lt;math xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML&quot;&gt;&lt;mstyle displaystyle=&quot;true&quot; display: inline-block;"><span style="display: inline-block; position: relative; width: 5.608em; height: 0px; font-size: 126%;"><span style="position: absolute; clip: rect(0.895em, 1005.56em, 3.127em, -999.998em); top: -2.279em; left: 0em;"><span class="mrow" id="MathJax-Span-247"><span class="mstyle" id="MathJax-Span-248"><span class="mrow" id="MathJax-Span-249"><span class="mfrac" id="MathJax-Span-250"><span style="display: inline-block; position: relative; width: 2.532em; height: 0px; margin-right: 0.102em; margin-left: 0.102em;"><span style="position: absolute; clip: rect(3.326em, 1002.38em, 4.318em, -999.998em); top: -4.71em; left: 50%; margin-left: -1.188em;"><span class="mrow" id="MathJax-Span-251"><span class="mi" id="MathJax-Span-252" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Italic;">𝑚</span><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-253" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular; padding-left: 0.25em;">−</span><span class="mi" id="MathJax-Span-254" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Italic; padding-left: 0.25em;">𝑛</span></span><span style="display: inline-block; width: 0px; height: 4.02em;"></span></span><span style="position: absolute; clip: rect(3.425em, 1000.7em, 4.169em, -999.998em); top: -3.321em; left: 50%; margin-left: -0.345em;"><span class="mi" id="MathJax-Span-255" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Italic;">𝑚</span><span style="display: inline-block; width: 0px; height: 4.02em;"></span></span><span style="position: absolute; clip: rect(0.846em, 1002.53em, 1.193em, -999.998em); top: -1.238em; left: 0em;"><span style="display: inline-block; overflow: hidden; vertical-align: 0em; border-top: 1.3px solid; width: 2.532em; height: 0px;"></span><span style="display: inline-block; width: 0px; height: 1.044em;"></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-256" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular;     <li style="text-align: left; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16">if first probe fails, probability second probe successful: <span class="nolink" data-asw-orgfontsize="16" style="font-size: 16px;"><span class="MathJax_Preview" style="color: inherit;"></span><span class="MathJax" id="MathJax-Element-22-Frame" tabindex="0" data-mathml="&lt;math xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML&quot;&gt;&lt;mstyle displaystyle=&quot;true&quot; scriptlevel=&quot;0&quot;&gt;&lt;mfrac&gt;&lt;mrow&gt;&lt;mi&gt;m&lt;/mi&gt;&lt;mo&gt;&amp;#x2212;&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;mi&gt;n&lt;/mi&gt;&lt;/mrow&gt;&lt;mi&gt;m&lt;/mi&gt;&lt;/mfrac&gt;&lt;/mstyle&gt;&lt;mo&gt;=&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;mi&gt;p&lt;/mi&gt;&lt;/math&gt;" role="presentation" style="position: relative;"><nobr aria-hidden="true"><span class="math" id="MathJax-Span-259" style="width: 10.568em;         <br>(one bad slot already found, <em>m − n</em> good slots remain and the second probe is
        uniformly random over the <em>m − 1</em> total slots left)
    </li>

        <br>(since two bad slots already found, <em>m−n </em>good slots remain and the third probe
        is uniformly random over the <em>m − 2</em> total slots left)&nbsp;
    </li>
    <li style="text-align: left; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16">...&nbsp;</li>
</ul>
<p data-asw-orgfontsize="16" style="font-size: 16px;">⇒ Every trial, success with probability at least <em>p</em>.</p>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16">Expected Number of trials for success?&nbsp;</p>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: center; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16"><span class="nolink" data-asw-orgfontsize="16" style="font-size: 16px;"><span class="MathJax_Preview" style="color: inherit;"></span><span class="MathJax" id="MathJax-Element-24-Frame" tabindex="0" data-mathml="&lt;math xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML&quot;&gt;&lt;mstyle displaystyle=&quot;true&quot; vertical-align: 0em; border-top: 1.3px solid; width: 0.598em; height: 0px;"></span><span style="display: inline-block; width: 0px; height: 1.044em;"></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-314" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular;     = \dfrac{1}{1 − α}</script></span>. <br></p>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16">With a little thought it follows that search, delete take time <span class="nolink" data-asw-orgfontsize="16" style="font-size: 16px;"><span class="MathJax_Preview" style="color: inherit;"></span><span class="MathJax" id="MathJax-Element-25-Frame" tabindex="0" data-mathml="&lt;math xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML&quot;&gt;&lt;mi&gt;O&lt;/mi&gt;&lt;mo stretchy=&quot;false&quot;&gt;(&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;mn&gt;1&lt;/mn&gt;&lt;mrow class=&quot;MJX-TeXAtom-ORD&quot;&gt;&lt;mo&gt;/&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;/mrow&gt;&lt;mo stretchy=&quot;false&quot;&gt;(&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;mn&gt;1&lt;/mn&gt;&lt;mo&gt;&amp;#x2212;&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;mrow class=&quot;MJX-TeXAtom-ORD&quot;&gt;&lt;mo&gt;&amp;#x3B1;&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;/mrow&gt;&lt;mo stretchy=&quot;false&quot;&gt;)&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;mo stretchy=&quot;false&quot;&gt;)&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;/math&gt;" role="presentation" style="position: relative;"><nobr aria-hidden="true"><span class="math" id="MathJax-Span-325" style="width: 6.352em; padding-left: 0.25em;">−</span><span class="texatom" id="MathJax-Span-336" style="padding-left: 0.25em;"><span class="mrow" id="MathJax-Span-337"><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-338" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular;">α</span></span></span><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-339" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular;">)</span><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-340" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular;">)</span></span><span style="display: inline-block; width: 0px; height: 2.383em;"></span></span></span><span style="display: inline-block; overflow: hidden; vertical-align: -0.309em; border-left: 0px solid; width: 0px; height: 1.191em;"></span></span></nobr><span class="MJX_Assistive_MathML" role="presentation"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>O</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"><mo>/</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"><mo>α</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math></span></span><script type="math/tex" id="MathJax-Element-25">O(1/(1 − α))</script></span>. Ditto if
    we attempt to insert an item that is already there. <br></p>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16"><br></p>
<h3 dir="ltr" style="text-align: left; font-size: 24px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="24">Open Addressing vs. Chaining</h3>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16">Open Addressing: better cache performance <em>(better memory usage, no pointers
    needed)</em></p>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16">Chaining: less sensitive to hash functions<em> (OA requires extra care to avoid clustering)</em>
    and the load factor α<em> (OA degrades past 70% or so and in any event cannot
    support values larger than 1)</em></p>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16"><br></p>
<h4 dir="ltr" style="text-align: left; font-size: 20px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="20">Cryptographic Hashing</h4>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16">A cryptographic hash function is a deterministic procedure that takes an arbitrary
    block of data and returns a fixed-size bit string, the (cryptographic) hash value, such
    that an accidental or intentional change to the data will change the hash value. The
    data to be encoded is often called the <em>message</em>, and the hash value is sometimes called
    the <em>message digest</em> or simply digest.<br></p>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16">The ideal cryptographic hash function has the properties listed below. d is the
    number of bits in the output of the hash function. You can think of m as being 2<sup>d</sup>. d
    is typically 160 or more. These hash functions can be used to index hash tables, but
    they are typically used in computer security applications.</p>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16"><br></p>
<h4 dir="ltr" style="text-align: left; font-size: 20px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="20">Desirable Properties</h4>
<ol dir="ltr" data-asw-orgfontsize="16" style="font-size: 16px;">
    <li style="text-align: left; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16"><strong>One-Way (OW)</strong>: Infeasible, given <span class="nolink" data-asw-orgfontsize="16" style="font-size: 16px;"><span class="MathJax_Preview" style="color: inherit;"></span><span class="MathJax" id="MathJax-Element-26-Frame" tabindex="0" data-mathml="&lt;math xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML&quot;&gt;&lt;mi&gt;y&lt;/mi&gt;&lt;mo&gt;&amp;#x2208;&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;mi&gt;R&lt;/mi&gt;&lt;msup&gt;&lt;mrow class=&quot;MJX-TeXAtom-ORD&quot;&gt;&lt;mn&gt;0&lt;/mn&gt;&lt;mo&gt;,&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;mn&gt;1&lt;/mn&gt;&lt;/mrow&gt;&lt;mi&gt;d&lt;/mi&gt;&lt;/msup&gt;&lt;/math&gt;" role="presentation" style="position: relative;"><nobr aria-hidden="true"><span class="math" id="MathJax-Span-341" style="width: 5.31em; display: inline-block;"><span style="display: inline-block; position: relative; width: 4.219em; height: 0px; font-size: 126%;"><span style="position: absolute; clip: rect(1.243em, 1004.22em, 2.631em, -999.998em); top: -2.279em; left: 0em;"><span class="mrow" id="MathJax-Span-342"><span class="mi" id="MathJax-Span-343" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Italic;">𝑦</span><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-344" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular; padding-left: 0.3em;">∈</span><span class="mi" id="MathJax-Span-345" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Italic; padding-left: 0.3em;">𝑅</span><span class="msubsup" id="MathJax-Span-346"><span style="display: inline-block; position: relative; width: 1.887em; height: 0px;"><span style="position: absolute; clip: rect(3.177em, 1001.34em, 4.318em, -999.998em); top: -4.015em; left: 0em;"><span class="texatom" id="MathJax-Span-347"><span class="mrow" id="MathJax-Span-348"><span class="mn" id="MathJax-Span-349" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular;">0</span><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-350" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular;">,</span><span class="mn" id="MathJax-Span-351" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular; padding-left: 0.201em;">1</span></span></span><span style="display: inline-block; width: 0px; height: 4.02em;"></span></span><span style="position: absolute; top: -4.412em; left: 1.441em;"><span class="mi" id="MathJax-Span-352" style="font-size: 70.7%; font-family: STIXGeneral-Italic;">𝑑</span><span style="display: inline-block; width: 0px; height: 4.02em;"></span></span></span></span></span><span style="display: inline-block; width: 0px; height: 2.284em;"></span></span></span><span style="display: inline-block; overflow: hidden; vertical-align: -0.309em; border-left: 0px solid; width: 0px; height: 1.441em;"></span></span></nobr><span class="MJX_Assistive_MathML" role="presentation"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>R</mi><msup><mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>d</mi></msup></math></span></span><script type="math/tex" id="MathJax-Element-26">y ∈ R {0, 1}^d</script></span> to find any <span class="nolink" data-asw-orgfontsize="16" style="font-size: 16px;"><span class="MathJax_Preview" style="color: inherit;"></span><span class="MathJax" id="MathJax-Element-27-Frame" tabindex="0" data-mathml="&lt;math xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML&quot;&gt;&lt;mi&gt;x&lt;/mi&gt;&lt;mi&gt;s&lt;/mi&gt;&lt;mo&gt;.&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;mi&gt;t&lt;/mi&gt;&lt;mo&gt;.&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;mi&gt;h&lt;/mi&gt;&lt;mo stretchy=&quot;false&quot;&gt;(&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;mi&gt;x&lt;/mi&gt;&lt;mo stretchy=&quot;false&quot;&gt;)&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;mo&gt;=&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;mi&gt;y&lt;/mi&gt;&lt;/math&gt;" role="presentation" style="position: relative;"><nobr aria-hidden="true"><span class="math" id="MathJax-Span-353" style="width: 7.096em; display: inline-block;"><span style="display: inline-block; position: relative; width: 5.608em; height: 0px; font-size: 126%;"><span style="position: absolute; clip: rect(1.441em, 1005.61em, 2.631em, -999.998em); top: -2.279em; left: 0em;"><span class="mrow" id="MathJax-Span-354"><span class="mi" id="MathJax-Span-355" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Italic;">𝑥</span><span class="mi" id="MathJax-Span-356" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Italic;">𝑠</span><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-357" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular;">.</span><span class="mi" id="MathJax-Span-358" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Italic; padding-left: 0.201em;">ℎ</span><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-361" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular;">(</span><span class="mi" id="MathJax-Span-362" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Italic;">𝑥</span><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-363" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular;">)</span><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-364" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular; padding-left: 0.3em;">=</span><span class="mi" id="MathJax-Span-365" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Italic; padding-left: 0.3em;">𝑦</span></span><span style="display: inline-block; width: 0px; height: 2.284em;"></span></span></span><span style="display: inline-block; overflow: hidden; vertical-align: -0.309em; border-left: 0px solid; width: 0px; height: 1.191em;"></span></span></nobr><span class="MJX_Assistive_MathML" role="presentation"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mi>s</mi><mo>.</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>.</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>y</mi></math></span></span><script type="math/tex" id="MathJax-Element-27">x s.t. h(x) = y</script></span>.
        This means that if you choose a random d-bit vector, it is hard to find an
        input to the hash that produces that vector. This involves "inverting" the hash
        function.&nbsp;</li>
    <li style="text-align: left; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16"><strong>Collision-resistance (CR)</strong>: Infeasible to find <span class="nolink" data-asw-orgfontsize="16" style="font-size: 16px;"><span class="MathJax_Preview" style="color: inherit;"></span><span class="MathJax" id="MathJax-Element-28-Frame" tabindex="0" data-mathml="&lt;math xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML&quot;&gt;&lt;mi&gt;x&lt;/mi&gt;&lt;mo&gt;,&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;mi&gt;x&lt;/mi&gt;&lt;mrow class=&quot;MJX-TeXAtom-ORD&quot;&gt;&lt;mo&gt;&amp;#x2032;&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;/mrow&gt;&lt;mo&gt;,&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;mi&gt;s&lt;/mi&gt;&lt;mo&gt;.&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;mi&gt;t&lt;/mi&gt;&lt;mo&gt;.&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;mi&gt;x&lt;/mi&gt;&lt;mo&gt;=&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;mi&gt;x&lt;/mi&gt;&lt;mrow class=&quot;MJX-TeXAtom-ORD&quot;&gt;&lt;mo&gt;&amp;#x2032;&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;/mrow&gt;&lt;/math&gt;" role="presentation" style="position: relative;"><nobr aria-hidden="true"><span class="math" id="MathJax-Span-366" style="width: 8.038em; display: inline-block;"><span style="display: inline-block; position: relative; width: 6.352em; height: 0px; font-size: 126%;"><span style="position: absolute; clip: rect(1.441em, 1006.25em, 2.582em, -999.998em); top: -2.279em; left: 0em;"><span class="mrow" id="MathJax-Span-367"><span class="mi" id="MathJax-Span-368" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Italic;">𝑥</span><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-369" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular;">,</span><span class="mi" id="MathJax-Span-370" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Italic; padding-left: 0.201em;">𝑥</span><span class="texatom" id="MathJax-Span-371"><span class="mrow" id="MathJax-Span-372"><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-373" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular;">′</span></span></span><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-374" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular;">,</span><span class="mi" id="MathJax-Span-375" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Italic; padding-left: 0.201em;">𝑥</span><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-380" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular; padding-left: 0.3em;">=</span><span class="mi" id="MathJax-Span-381" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Italic; padding-left: 0.3em;">𝑥</span><span class="texatom" id="MathJax-Span-382"><span class="mrow" id="MathJax-Span-383"><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-384" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular;">′</span></span></span></span><span style="display: inline-block; width: 0px; height: 2.284em;"></span></span></span><span style="display: inline-block; overflow: hidden; vertical-align: -0.247em; border-left: 0px solid; width: 0px; height: 1.191em;"></span></span></nobr><span class="MJX_Assistive_MathML" role="presentation"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"><mo>′</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>.</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>.</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"><mo>′</mo></mrow></math></span></span><script type="math/tex" id="MathJax-Element-28">x, x′, s.t. x = x′</script></span> and <span class="nolink" data-asw-orgfontsize="16" style="font-size: 16px;"><span class="MathJax_Preview" style="color: inherit;"></span><span class="MathJax" id="MathJax-Element-29-Frame" tabindex="0" data-mathml="&lt;math xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML&quot;&gt;&lt;mi&gt;h&lt;/mi&gt;&lt;mo stretchy=&quot;false&quot;&gt;(&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;mi&gt;x&lt;/mi&gt;&lt;mo stretchy=&quot;false&quot;&gt;)&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;mo&gt;=&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;mi&gt;h&lt;/mi&gt;&lt;mo stretchy=&quot;false&quot;&gt;(&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;mi&gt;x&lt;/mi&gt;&lt;mrow class=&quot;MJX-TeXAtom-ORD&quot;&gt;&lt;mo&gt;&amp;#x2032;&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;/mrow&gt;&lt;mo stretchy=&quot;false&quot;&gt;)&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;/math&gt;" role="presentation" style="position: relative;"><nobr aria-hidden="true"><span class="math" id="MathJax-Span-385" style="width: 6.153em; display: inline-block;"><span style="display: inline-block; position: relative; width: 4.864em; height: 0px; font-size: 126%;"><span style="position: absolute; clip: rect(1.441em, 1004.81em, 2.631em, -999.998em); top: -2.279em; left: 0em;"><span class="mrow" id="MathJax-Span-386"><span class="mi" id="MathJax-Span-387" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Italic;">ℎ</span><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-388" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular;">(</span><span class="mi" id="MathJax-Span-389" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Italic;">𝑥</span><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-390" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular;">)</span><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-391" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular; padding-left: 0.3em;">=</span><span class="mi" id="MathJax-Span-392" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Italic; padding-left: 0.3em;">ℎ</span><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-393" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular;">(</span><span class="mi" id="MathJax-Span-394" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Italic;">𝑥</span><span class="texatom" id="MathJax-Span-395"><span class="mrow" id="MathJax-Span-396"><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-397" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular;">′</span></span></span><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-398" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular;">)</span></span><span style="display: inline-block; width: 0px; height: 2.284em;"></span></span></span><span style="display: inline-block; overflow: hidden; vertical-align: -0.309em; border-left: 0px solid; width: 0px; height: 1.191em;"></span></span></nobr><span class="MJX_Assistive_MathML" role="presentation"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"><mo>′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math></span></span><script type="math/tex" id="MathJax-Element-29">h(x) =
        h(x′)</script></span>. This is a collision, two input values have the same hash.&nbsp;</li>
    <li style="text-align: left; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16"><strong>Target collision-resistance (TCR)</strong>: Infeasible given x to find <span class="nolink" data-asw-orgfontsize="16" style="font-size: 16px;"><span class="MathJax_Preview" style="color: inherit;"></span><span class="MathJax" id="MathJax-Element-30-Frame" tabindex="0" data-mathml="&lt;math xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML&quot;&gt;&lt;mi&gt;x&lt;/mi&gt;&lt;mrow class=&quot;MJX-TeXAtom-ORD&quot;&gt;&lt;mo&gt;&amp;#x2032;&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;/mrow&gt;&lt;mo&gt;=&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;mi&gt;x&lt;/mi&gt;&lt;mi&gt;s&lt;/mi&gt;&lt;mo&gt;.&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;mi&gt;t&lt;/mi&gt;&lt;mo&gt;.&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;mi&gt;h&lt;/mi&gt;&lt;mo stretchy=&quot;false&quot;&gt;(&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;mi&gt;x&lt;/mi&gt;&lt;mo stretchy=&quot;false&quot;&gt;)&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;mo&gt;=&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;mi&gt;h&lt;/mi&gt;&lt;mo stretchy=&quot;false&quot;&gt;(&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;mi&gt;x&lt;/mi&gt;&lt;mrow class=&quot;MJX-TeXAtom-ORD&quot;&gt;&lt;mo&gt;&amp;#x2032;&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;/mrow&gt;&lt;mo stretchy=&quot;false&quot;&gt;)&lt;/mo&gt;&lt;/math&gt;" role="presentation" style="position: relative;"><nobr aria-hidden="true"><span class="math" id="MathJax-Span-399" style="width: 11.312em; display: inline-block;"><span style="display: inline-block; position: relative; width: 8.981em; height: 0px; font-size: 126%;"><span style="position: absolute; clip: rect(1.441em, 1008.93em, 2.631em, -999.998em); top: -2.279em; left: 0em;"><span class="mrow" id="MathJax-Span-400"><span class="mi" id="MathJax-Span-401" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Italic;">𝑥</span><span class="texatom" id="MathJax-Span-402"><span class="mrow" id="MathJax-Span-403"><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-404" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular;">′</span></span></span><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-405" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular; padding-left: 0.3em;">=</span><span class="mi" id="MathJax-Span-406" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Italic; padding-left: 0.3em;">𝑥</span><span class="mi" id="MathJax-Span-407" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Italic;">𝑠</span><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-408" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular;">.</span><span class="mi" id="MathJax-Span-409" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Italic; padding-left: 0.201em;">𝑡</span><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-410" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular;">.</span><span class="mi" id="MathJax-Span-411" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Italic; padding-left: 0.201em;">ℎ</span><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-412" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular;">(</span><span class="mi" id="MathJax-Span-413" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Italic;">𝑥</span><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-414" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular;">)</span><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-415" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular; padding-left: 0.3em;">=</span><span class="mi" id="MathJax-Span-416" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Italic; padding-left: 0.3em;">ℎ</span><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-417" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular;">(</span><span class="mi" id="MathJax-Span-418" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Italic;">𝑥</span><span class="texatom" id="MathJax-Span-419"><span class="mrow" id="MathJax-Span-420"><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-421" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular;">′</span></span></span><span class="mo" id="MathJax-Span-422" style="font-family: STIXGeneral-Regular;">)</span></span><span style="display: inline-block; width: 0px; height: 2.284em;"></span></span></span><span style="display: inline-block; overflow: hidden; vertical-align: -0.309em; border-left: 0px solid; width: 0px; height: 1.191em;"></span></span></nobr><span class="MJX_Assistive_MathML" role="presentation"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"><mo>′</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mi>s</mi><mo>.</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>.</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mrow class="MJX-TeXAtom-ORD"><mo>′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math></span></span><script type="math/tex" id="MathJax-Element-30">x′ = x s.t.
        h(x) = h(x′)</script></span>.</li>
</ol>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16">TCR is weaker than CR. If a hash function satisfies CR, it automatically satisfies
    TCR. There is no implication relationship between OW and CR/TCR.</p>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16"><br></p>
<h3 dir="ltr" style="text-align: left; font-size: 24px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="24">Applications</h3>
<ol dir="ltr" data-asw-orgfontsize="16" style="font-size: 16px;">
    <li style="text-align: left; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16"><strong>Password storage</strong>: Store <em>h(P W)</em>, not <em>PW </em>on computer. When user inputs
        <em>PW′</em>, compute <em>h(PW′) </em>and compare against <em>h(PW)</em>. The property required of
        the hash function is OW. The adversary does not know <em>PW </em>or <em>PW′</em> so TCR
        or CR is not really required. Of course, if many, many passwords have the
        same hash, it is a problem, but a small number of collisions doesn't really affect
        security.</li>
    <li style="text-align: left; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16"><strong>File modification detector</strong>: For each file F , store<em> h(F)</em> securely. Check if F
        is modified by recomputing <em>h(F)</em>. The property that is required is TCR, since
        the adversary wins if he/she is able to modify F without changing <em>h(F)</em>.&nbsp;</li>
    <li style="text-align: left; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16"><strong>Digital signatures</strong>: In public-key cryptography, Alice has a public key PK<sub>A</sub>
        and a private key SK<sub>A</sub>. Alice can sign a message M using her private key
        to produce σ = sign(SK<sub>A</sub>, M). Anyone who knows Alice's public key PK<sub>A</sub>
        and verify Alice's signature by checking that verify (M, σ, PK<sub>A</sub>) is true. The
        adversary wants to forge a signature that verifies. For large M it is easier to
        sign h(M) rather than M , i.e., σ = sign(SK<sub>A</sub>, h(M)). The property that we require is CR. We don't want an adversary to ask Alice to sign x and then claim
        that she signed x′, where <em>h(x) = h(x′)</em>.</li>
</ol>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16"><br></p>
<h3 dir="ltr" style="text-align: left; font-size: 24px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="24">Implementations</h3>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left; font-size: 16px;" data-asw-orgfontsize="16">There have been many proposals for hash functions which are OW, CR and TCR.
    Some of these have been broken. MD-5, for example, has been shown to not be CR.
    There is a competition underway to determine SHA-3, which would be a Secure Hash
    Algorithm certified by NIST. Cryptographic hash functions are significantly more
    complex than those used in hash tables. You can think of a cryptographic hash as
    running a regular hash function many, many times with pseudo-random permutations
    interspersed.<br></p></span></div></div></div>

        <section id="region-main" aria-label="Content">
            <span class="notifications" id="user-notifications"></span>

                <div class="activity-header" data-for="page-activity-header">

            <div role="main"><div id="mod_book-chaptersnavigation"><div class="container-fluid tertiary-navigation">
    <div class="row">
            <div class="navitem">
                <a class="btn btn-link btn-previous" href="https://learn.saylor.org/mod/book/view.php?id=96107&amp;chapterid=90521#mod_book-chapter" title="Previous" aria-label="Previous">
                    <i class="icon fa fa-chevron-left fa-fw " aria-hidden="true" ></i>

    </div>
</div></div><div id="mod_book-chapter" class="box py-3 generalbox book_content"><h3>Hashing II</h3><div class="no-overflow"><span class="filter_mathjaxloader_equation"><h4 dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;">Lecture Overview</h4>
<ul dir="ltr">
    <li style="text-align: left;">Table Resizing&nbsp;</li>
    <li style="text-align: left;">Amortization</li>
    <li style="text-align: left;">String Matching and Karp-Rabin</li>
    <li style="text-align: left;">Rolling Hash&nbsp;</li>
</ul>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;"><br></p>
<h3 dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;">Recall:</h3>
<h4 dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;">Hashing with Chaining:</h4>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: center;"><img src="https://learn.saylor.org/pluginfile.php/10439571/mod_book/chapter/90522/Screenshot%202024-04-27%20at%2008-27-59%206.006%20Lecture%2009%20Table%20doubling%20Karp-Rabin%20-%20160b3b5f9da2e03815ca1e6ee0dba62a_MIT6_006F11_lec09.pdf.png" alt="Figure 1: Hashing with Chaining" width="546" height="193" class="img-fluid atto_image_button_text-bottom"><br></p>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: center;"><strong>Figure 1: </strong>Hashing with Chaining</p>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;">Expected cost (insert/delete/search): <span class="nolink">\(Θ(1 + α)\)</span>, assuming simple uniform hashing OR
    universal hashing &amp; hash function <span class="nolink">\(h\)</span> takes <span class="nolink">\(O(1)\)</span> time. <br></p>
<h4 dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;">Division Method:</h4>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: center;"><span class="nolink">\(h(k) = k \text{ mod }m\)</span></p>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;">where m is ideally prime</p>
<h4 dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;">Multiplication Method:</h4>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: center;"><span class="nolink">\(h(k) = [(a · k) \text{ mod }2^w] &gt; (w − r)\)</span></p>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;">where a is a random odd integer between <span class="nolink">\(2^{w−1}\)</span> and <span class="nolink">\(2^w, k\)</span> is given by <span class="nolink">\(w\)</span> bits, and <span class="nolink">\(m\)</span> = table
    size = <span class="nolink">\(2^r\)</span>.</p>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;"><br></p>
<h4 dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;">How Large should Table be?&nbsp;</h4>
<ul dir="ltr">
    <li style="text-align: left;">want <span class="nolink">\(m = Θ(n)\)</span> at all times</li>
    <li style="text-align: left;">don't know how large n will get at creation</li>
    <li style="text-align: left;"><span class="nolink">\(m\)</span> too small ⇒ slow; <span class="nolink">\(m\)</span> too big ⇒ wasteful</li>
</ul>
<h5 dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;">Idea:</h5>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;">Start small (constant) and grow (or shrink) as necessary.</p>
<h4 dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;">Rehashing:</h4>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;">To grow or shrink table hash function must change (m, r)&nbsp;</p>
<div style="margin-left: 30px;" class="editor-indent">
    <p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;">⇒ must rebuild hash table from scratch</p>
    <div style="margin-left: 30px;" class="editor-indent">
        <p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;">for item in old table: → for each slot, for item in slot</p>
        <div style="margin-left: 30px;" class="editor-indent">
            <p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;">insert into new table&nbsp;</p>
        </div>
    </div>
    <p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;">⇒ <span class="nolink">\(Θ(n + m)\)</span> time = <span class="nolink">\(Θ(n)\)</span> if <span class="nolink">\(m = Θ(n)\)</span></p>
    <p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;"><br></p>
</div>
<h4 dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;">How fast to grow?</h4>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;">When <span class="nolink">\(n\)</span> reaches <span class="nolink">\(m\)</span>, say</p>
<ul dir="ltr">
    <li style="text-align: left;"><span class="nolink">\(m + =1\)</span>? <br>⇒ rebuild every step<br>⇒ <span class="nolink">\(n\)</span> inserts cost <span class="nolink">\(Θ(1 + 2 + · · · + n) = Θ(n^2)\)</span><br></li>
    <li style="text-align: left;"><span class="nolink">\(m ∗ =2? m = Θ(n)\)</span> still <span class="nolink">\((r+ =1)\)</span><br>⇒ rebuild at insertion <span class="nolink">\(2^i\)</span> <br>⇒ <span class="nolink">\(n\)</span> inserts cost <span class="nolink">\(Θ(1 + 2 + 4 + 8 + · · · + n)\)</span> where <span class="nolink">\(n\)</span> is really the next power of <span class="nolink">\(2
        = Θ(n)\)</span></li>
    <li style="text-align: left;">a few inserts cost linear time, but <span class="nolink">\(Θ(1)\)</span> "on average".&nbsp;</li>
</ul>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;"><br></p>
<h3 dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;">Amortized Analysis</h3>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;">This is a common technique in data structures - like paying rent: $1500/month ≈ $50/day</p>
<ul dir="ltr">
    <li style="text-align: left;">operation has <u>amortized cost</u> <span class="nolink">\(T(n)\)</span> if <span class="nolink">\(k\)</span> operations cost <span class="nolink">\(≤ k · T (n)\)</span> <br></li>
    <li style="text-align: left;">"<span class="nolink">\(T(n)\)</span> amortized" roughly means <span class="nolink">\(T(n)\)</span> "on average", but averaged over all ops.</li>
    <li style="text-align: left;">e.g. inserting into a hash table takes <span class="nolink">\(O(1)\)</span> amortized time.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;"><br></p>
<h3 dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;">Back to Hashing:</h3>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;">Maintain <span class="nolink">\(m = Θ(n)\)</span> ⇒ <span class="nolink">\(α = Θ(1)\)</span> ⇒ support search in <span class="nolink">\(O(1)\)</span> expected time (assuming
    simple uniform or universal hashing)&nbsp;</p>
<h5 dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;">Delete:</h5>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;">Also <span class="nolink">\(O(1)\)</span> expected as is.&nbsp;</p>
<ul dir="ltr">
    <li style="text-align: left;">space can get big with respect to <span class="nolink">\(n\)</span> e.g. <span class="nolink">\(n×\)</span> insert, <span class="nolink">\(n×\)</span> delete</li>
    <li style="text-align: left;"><u>solution:</u> when <span class="nolink">\(n\)</span> decreases to m/4, shrink to half the size ⇒ <span class="nolink">\(O(1)\)</span> amortized cost
        for both insert and delete - analysis is harder.&nbsp;</li>
</ul>
<h5 dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;">Resizable Arrays:</h5>
<ul dir="ltr">
    <li style="text-align: left;">same trick solves Python "list" (array)&nbsp;</li>
    <li style="text-align: left;">⇒ list.append and list.pop in <span class="nolink">\(O(1)\)</span> amortized</li>
</ul>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: center;"><img src="https://learn.saylor.org/pluginfile.php/10439571/mod_book/chapter/90522/Screenshot%202024-04-27%20at%2008-33-14%206.006%20Lecture%2009%20Table%20doubling%20Karp-Rabin%20-%20160b3b5f9da2e03815ca1e6ee0dba62a_MIT6_006F11_lec09.pdf.png" alt="Figure 2: Resizeable Arrays" width="396" height="95" class="img-fluid atto_image_button_text-bottom"><br></p>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: center;"><strong>Figure 2:</strong> Resizeable Arrays</p>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;"><br></p>
<h3 dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;">String Matching</h3>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;">Given two strings <span class="nolink">\(s\)</span> and <span class="nolink">\(t\)</span>, does <span class="nolink">\(s\)</span> occur as a substring of <span class="nolink">\(t\)</span>? (and if so, where and how many
    times?)</p>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;">E.g. s = '6.006' and t = your entire INBOX ('grep' on UNIX)</p>
<h5 dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;">Simple Algorithm:</h5>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;">any(s == t[i : i + len(s)] for i in range(len(t) − len(s)))&nbsp;</p>
<div style="margin-left: 30px;" class="editor-indent">
    <p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;">- O(|s|) time for each substring comparison&nbsp;</p>
    <p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;">⇒ O(|s| · (|t| − |s|)) time&nbsp;</p>
    <p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;">= O(|s| · |t|) potentially quadratic<br></p>
</div>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: center;"><img src="https://learn.saylor.org/pluginfile.php/10439571/mod_book/chapter/90522/Screenshot%202024-04-27%20at%2008-34-08%206.006%20Lecture%2009%20Table%20doubling%20Karp-Rabin%20-%20160b3b5f9da2e03815ca1e6ee0dba62a_MIT6_006F11_lec09.pdf.png" alt="Figure 3: Illustration of Simple Algorithm for the String Matching Problem " width="367" height="121" class="img-fluid atto_image_button_text-bottom"><br></p>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: center;"><strong>Figure 3: </strong>Illustration of Simple Algorithm for the String Matching Problem <br></p>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: center;"><br></p>
<h5 dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;">Karp-Rabin Algorithm:</h5>
<ul dir="ltr">
    <li style="text-align: left;">Compare <span class="nolink">\(h(s) == h(t[i : i + len(s)])\)</span><br></li>
    <li style="text-align: left;">If hash values match, likely so do strings<ul>
            <li style="text-align: left;">can check <span class="nolink">\(s == t[i : i + len(s)] \)</span> to be sure <span class="nolink">\(∼ cost O(|s|) \)</span></li>
            <li style="text-align: left;">if yes, found match - done
                1&nbsp;</li>
            <li style="text-align: left;">if no, happened with probability <span class="nolink">\(&lt;\dfrac{1}{|s|}\)</span><br>⇒ expected cost is <span class="nolink">\(O(1)\)</span> per <em>i</em>.&nbsp;</li>
        </ul>
    </li>
    <li style="text-align: left;">need suitable hash function.&nbsp;</li>
    <li style="text-align: left;">expected time <span class="nolink">\(= O(|s| + |t| · cost(h))\)</span>.&nbsp;<ul>
            <li style="text-align: left;">naively <span class="nolink">\(h(x)\)</span> costs <span class="nolink">\(|x|\)</span><br></li>
            <li style="text-align: left;">we'll achieve <span class="nolink">\(O(1)! \)</span></li>
            <li style="text-align: left;">idea: <span class="nolink">\(t[i : i + len(s)] ≈ t[i + 1 : i + 1 + len(s)]\)</span>.&nbsp;</li>
        </ul>
    </li>
</ul>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;"><br></p>
<h3 dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;">Rolling Hash ADT</h3>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;">Maintain string x subject to&nbsp;</p>
<ul dir="ltr">
    <li style="text-align: left;"><u>r()</u>: reasonable hash function <span class="nolink">\(h(x)\)</span> on string <span class="nolink">\(x\)</span></li>
    <li style="text-align: left;"><u>r.append(c)</u>: add letter <span class="nolink">\(c\)</span> to end of string <span class="nolink">\(x\)</span><br></li>
    <li style="text-align: left;"><u>r.skip(c)</u>: remove front letter from string <span class="nolink">\(x\)</span>, assuming it is <span class="nolink">\(c\)</span> <br></li>
</ul>
<p><br></p>
<h5 dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;">Karp-Rabin Application:</h5>
<pre class="prettyprint prettyprinted" style=""><span class="kwd">for</span><span class="pln"> c </span><span class="kwd">in</span><span class="pln"> s</span><span class="pun">:</span><span class="pln"> rs</span><span class="pun">.</span><span class="pln">append</span><span class="pun">(</span><span class="pln">c</span><span class="pun">)</span><br><span class="kwd">for</span><span class="pln"> c </span><span class="kwd">in</span><span class="pln"> t</span><span class="pun">[:</span><span class="pln">len</span><span class="pun">(</span><span class="pln">s</span><span class="pun">)]:</span><span class="pln"> rt</span><span class="pun">.</span><span class="pln">append</span><span class="pun">(</span><span class="pln">c</span><span class="pun">)</span><br><span class="kwd">if</span><span class="pln"> rs</span><span class="pun">()</span><span class="pln"> </span><span class="pun">==</span><span class="pln"> rt</span><span class="pun">():</span><span class="pln"> </span><span class="pun">...</span><br></pre>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;">This first block of code is <span class="nolink">\(O(|s|)\)</span> <br></p>
<pre class="prettyprint prettyprinted" style=""><span class="kwd">for</span><span class="pln"> i </span><span class="kwd">in</span><span class="pln"> range</span><span class="pun">(</span><span class="pln">len</span><span class="pun">(</span><span class="pln">s</span><span class="pun">),</span><span class="pln"> len</span><span class="pun">(</span><span class="pln">t</span><span class="pun">)):</span><span class="pln"> </span><br><span class="pln">rt</span><span class="pun">.</span><span class="pln">skip</span><span class="pun">(</span><span class="pln">t</span><span class="pun">[</span><span class="pln">i</span><span class="pun">-</span><span class="pln">len</span><span class="pun">(</span><span class="pln">s</span><span class="pun">)])</span><span class="pln"> </span><br><span class="pln">rt</span><span class="pun">.</span><span class="pln">append</span><span class="pun">(</span><span class="pln">t</span><span class="pun">[</span><span class="pln">i</span><span class="pun">])</span><span class="pln"> </span><br><span class="kwd">if</span><span class="pln"> rs</span><span class="pun">()</span><span class="pln"> </span><span class="pun">==</span><span class="pln"> rt</span><span class="pun">():</span><span class="pln"> </span><span class="pun">...</span><span class="pln"> </span><br></pre>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;"><br></p><p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;">The second block of code is O(|t|) + O(# matches − |s|) to verify. <br></p>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;"><br></p>
<h4 dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;">Data Structure:</h4>
<p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;">Treat string <span class="nolink">\(x\)</span> as a multidigit number u in base a where a denotes the alphabet size, e.g.,
    256&nbsp;</p>
<ul dir="ltr">
    <li style="text-align: left;"><em>r() = u</em> mod p for (ideally random) prime <span class="nolink">\(p ≈ |s|\)</span> or <span class="nolink">\(|t|\)</span> (<u>division method</u>)&nbsp;</li>
    <li style="text-align: left;"><span class="nolink">\(r\)</span> stores <span class="nolink">\(u \text {mod }p\)</span> and <span class="nolink">\(|x|\)</span> (really <span class="nolink">\(a|^x|\)</span>), not <span class="nolink">\(u\)</span> <br>⇒ smaller and faster to work with (<span class="nolink">\(u \text{ mod }p\)</span> fits in one machine word)&nbsp;</li>
    <li style="text-align: left;"><em>r.append(c): (u · a + ord(c)) mod p = [(u mod p) · a + ord(c)] mod p&nbsp;</em></li>
    <li style="text-align: left;"><em>r.skip(c): [u − ord(c) · (a<sup>|u|−1</sup> mod p)] mod p
            <br>= [(u mod p) − ord(c) · (a<sup>|x−1|</sup> mod p)] mod p</em></li>
</ul></span></div></div><div class="flexsections-activity-page-navigate-back">
        <div class="header backto">
            <a href="https://learn.saylor.org/course/view.php?id=1307#section-36">
                <i class="icon fa fa-arrow-up fa-fw " aria-hidden="true"></i>
                Back to '8.1: Hash Tables\'
            </a>
        </div>
</div></div>
            
            

        </section>
    </div>
</div>




</div>
    </div>
    </div>

<script>
    document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () {
        const playlistItems = document.querySelectorAll('.playlist-item');
        const currentVideo = document.getElementById('current-video');
        const videoIds = Array.from(playlistItems).map(item => item.getAttribute('data-video'));
        let currentIndex = 0;

        const updateActiveItem = () => {
            playlistItems.forEach(item => item.classList.remove('active'));
            if (playlistItems[currentIndex]) {
                playlistItems[currentIndex].classList.add('active');
            }
        };

        playlistItems.forEach((item, index) => {
            item.addEventListener('click', function () {
                currentIndex = index;
                const videoId = this.getAttribute('data-video');
                if (currentVideo) {
                    currentVideo.src = `https://www.youtube.com/embed/${videoId}?autoplay=1`;
                    updateActiveItem();
                }
            });
        });

        if (currentVideo) {
            currentVideo.addEventListener('ended', function () {
                currentIndex = (currentIndex + 1) % videoIds.length;
                currentVideo.src = `https://www.youtube.com/embed/${videoIds[currentIndex]}?autoplay=1`;
                updateActiveItem();
            });
        }

        updateActiveItem();
    });
</script>

                <span id="maincontent"></span>
